video_title: Warriors Talks on Jaylen Brown Were Brief and Dead" — Anthony Slater

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors prioritized Anthony Melton over other free agent options
quotes.excerpt: There was definitely a De'Anthony Simons or De'Anthony Melton type conversation. They preferred Melton.
quotes.quote: There was definitely a De'Anthony Simons or De'Anthony Melton type conversation. They preferred Melton. Rui Hachimura is a guy that they looked at. They wouldn't have gone to the full mid-level type number that they were willing to get to for LeBron James because again that would have cost Moses Moody on a trade and then a Draymond Green pay cut that clearly Draymond was executing only for LeBron James.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors never realistically pursued LeBron James in free agency
quotes.excerpt: I didn't even think we were realistically in the running for LeBron. It never seemed serious.
quotes.quote: Steve Kerr said, 'I didn't even think we were realistically in the running for LeBron. It just never seemed serious to me, despite all the reports.'

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors were pessimistic about their chances of landing LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: I was reporting through the entire process how pessimistic they felt and the signals they were not getting.
quotes.quote: I was reporting through the entire process how pessimistic they felt and the signals they were not getting. Part of the hints they were not getting is the intel being gathered from a Draymond Green who is on vacation. Steve Kerr had his conversation with him. LeBron James had a conversation with Nick Nurse. He had a bunch of conversations with Sixers people in the lead up to ultimately finally deciding yes. The Warriors did not have those conversations. Steve Kerr did not talk once to LeBron James during this process.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors prioritized team building over chasing star free agents
quotes.excerpt: There wasn't any trades or any free agents they didn't get because they waited on LeBron James.
quotes.quote: There wasn't any trades or any free agents they didn't get because they waited on LeBron James. He was to them a minimum guy. Obviously a high-profile minimum guy, but just a minimum guy deciding to go elsewhere. They move on. It was to them like a minimum guy, obviously a high-profile minimum guy, but just a minimum guy deciding to go elsewhere. They move on.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors' interest in Jaylen Brown was brief and non-serious
quotes.excerpt: Boston wasn't looking to trade Brown at all. He is having a sixth and MVP voting season.
quotes.quote: Boston wasn't looking to trade Brown at all. He is having a sixth and MVP voting season. It was around the draft. Obviously it was around the Giannis Antetokounmpo heat up conversations and as Boston is actually deciding to canvas the league on Brown, right? It isn't just oh they had some high-level conversations with the Warriors. It sounds like they called around the league. I think that's well known. The Warriors conversation was extremely brief, extremely dead right away.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: NBA tanking rules have shifted, reducing interest in expiring contracts
quotes.excerpt: The tanking rules have shifted. There are far fewer teams that say, sure, we'll take $54 million.
quotes.quote: The tanking rules have shifted. There are far fewer teams that say, sure, we'll take $54 million of zero production next year because so many more teams next season actually want to win, including teams like the Wizards, the Jazz, the Pacers, all those teams. So it's very low value for the type of player Jimmy Butler theoretically is and was, because he is not going to help your team and he is a huge price tag in the apron era.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Stephen Curry's focus is on health and internal growth
quotes.excerpt: Most importantly for him is to make sure that knee and body is as right as possible.
quotes.quote: For Stephen Curry moving forward, I think most importantly for him is to make sure that knee and body is as right as possible as he enters his age 38 season. Try to be as productive and healthy as possible early on. I think collectively as a team, there is a belief that they can have some internal growth and maybe surprise early in the season.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors front office remains highly collaborative and respectful
quotes.excerpt: I've been given no indication it's anything different than it's always been, which is highly respected.
quotes.quote: I've been given no indication it's anything different than it's always been, which is highly respected on both sides, communication, particularly from Stephen Curry to Steve Kerr, Stephen Curry to Mike Dunleavy. It used to be Bob Myers, that's typically how it's been in the offseasons. Mike doesn't overly bother Stephen Curry, but for big news or big recruitments, Stephen Curry should probably be called by Stephen Curry within this recruitment process. Stephen Curry mostly operates to himself during the off-season.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green's contract includes an implicit no-trade clause
quotes.excerpt: He would have had this like it's called an implicit no-trade clause.
quotes.quote: Technically because it was an opt-out and then a resign, he would have had this like it's called an implicit no-trade clause. You guys might remember during the Jonathan Kuminga saga of last summer that was within the negotiations was the Warriors trying to get him on the one plus one but waive the implicit no-trade, which by the way they got him to. Part of why he was traded. With Draymond Green, same thing and part of the negotiation there was just essentially, hey, you are getting you are coming back on the exact same contract that you would have opted into.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Dunleavy has built a solid track record with draft picks
quotes.excerpt: I think it's fair to point out Mike Dunleavy's drafts have been good.
quotes.quote: I think it's fair to point out Mike Dunleavy's drafts have been good. Your Brandin Podziemski was Dunleavy's first first-round pick. Trayce Jackson-Davis, the 50s picks, right? Will Richard or Quinten Post. He is building a solid early track record on picks. Number one, two as far as the flexibility, sure, I think it's fair to wonder, hey, post-Stephen Curry, is this going to be an appealing destination? Has it even been an appealing destination in the current moment? They've been turning down by a lot of guys. I think that's fair to point out.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Teams are using cap space to trade for stars
quotes.excerpt: Look what Washington did last year, right? They had a bunch of future room.
quotes.quote: Look what Washington did last year, right? They had a bunch of future room and they decided to trade for Trae Young and trade for Anthony Davis. Even though particularly on the Davis run, Anthony Davis did not want to go to Washington. Washington just decided we will grab him because we have the room to get him and have that big contract here because they had no big contracts into the future. Utah did it with Jaren Jackson Jr., right? They grabbed Jaren Jackson Jr. from Memphis for a few first-round picks. It's not because Jaren Jackson Jr. chose to go to the Utah Jazz, it's because Utah had a bunch of flexibility, finally decided to cash in.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Lacob is a highly involved owner in decision-making
quotes.excerpt: He is certainly more involved than your typical owner.
quotes.quote: I understand that Joe Lacob is like the face of the decision-making tree and he is certainly more involved than your typical owner, right? You are not going to many war rooms live with the team on the clock and the owner is in a spirited debate with the GM. Like, it's not happening in a lot of places. Now, the Mike Dunleavy embraces that. Bob Myers previously embraced it. Some would say, hey, like part of the reason that Bob, you know, tired of the job was because of it.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Lacob's spending habits are highly regarded by team staff
quotes.excerpt: One of the, I would say the number one thing that they love about Joe Lacob is the way he spends.
quotes.quote: You talk to people who like have have been in other organizations and and now are under Joe Lacob, one of the, I would say the number one thing that they love about Joe Lacob is the way he spends. I mean, he spent outrageous amounts of money into the tax over the last decade and I'm not just talking about like paying tax, I'm talking about paying for staff, I'm talking about filling your, you know, like training staff and the hotels they stay on the road and the team dinners they have. Like they are a very plush organization.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Lacob is involved but not a dictator
quotes.excerpt: He is not a dictator overrule whatever. Like he does, you know, really allow his people to make decisions.
quotes.quote: I say process, he is not a dictator overrule whatever. Like he does, you know, really allow his people to make decisions, but he is very much in the conversations and he is very much open that he is in the conversations and that is different than for example a Clay Bennett in Oklahoma City. That's very different.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Brandin Podziemski's draft process showed maturity
quotes.excerpt: He was probably like fringe first, probably maybe a second-round pick. Warriors interviewed him.
quotes.quote: He was probably like fringe first, probably maybe a second-round pick. Warriors interviewed him. He bombed the interview, according to him, or according to the Warriors who told him he bombed the interview. Went to Michigan. Really you can tell learned a lot at Michigan, right? That's a serious program, winning habits. They obviously go on to win the national championship and you can tell the Warriors, despite him still in some ways being a goofball, were like, oh, this is a matured player and a matured individual when they did the draft process the second time around. Obviously they decided to draft him. And then I would say one of the things to your point on his personality, he really won Steve Kerr over in this process.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Warriors need to prioritize Brandin Podziemski's development
quotes.excerpt: They may have a new starting wing to start next year, or at least a high minutes guy.
quotes.quote: They may have a new starting wing to start next year, or at least a high minutes guy. And I think we will view this off-season a little differently if Brandin Podziemski becomes like a really big-time pick at 11. I don't know if that's the case, but it would it would be viewed differently.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Brandin Podziemski's development is a priority for the Warriors
quotes.excerpt: I think training camp will matter. I think Gui Santos, the comfort level with him.
quotes.quote: I think training camp will matter. I think Gui Santos, the comfort level with him and like how many games he started last year. I in no ways think it's some like, oh, lock it in or he is the favorite. But if he plays extremely well in camp, they have a need because of the injuries on the wing, and I do think they want to fast-forward his developmental process. That's one thing you get when you talk to them is like, you know, some of the pains of the past and and how they didn't maybe develop guys as well as they could have. Like they want to get it right this time around.
